Candidate cycle: 1 -f-> 2 -g-> 3 -h-> 1. Check: f is enabled at states 0,1,2,3 (x too). The cycle 1→2→3→1 has NO x-edge → SF(x) is VIOLATED (x is enabled at infinitely many visited states, but no x-edges ever taken) → so that cycle is NOT fair → the whole graph is non-terminating only if some fair cycle exists elsewhere. Since every non-done state has an x-edge to the done state, any infinite run staying in non-done states has x enabled at every visited state → SF(x) violated → so terminates=True ✓. My implementation says True ✓ and brute force says True ✓. My test expectation was wrong (I added those x edges to all states without thinking).
